findings.text: follow-on: the two gate logs recorded as baseline_suite/after_suite differ by two failing ids — tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py::test_collect_catalog_changes and tests/standard_names/test_review_release.py::test_pr_target_derived_from_remotes fail at head (head-importers.log, 22 failed) and pass at base (base-importers.log, 30 failed + 3 errors). The run's manifest reports the importer gate as adding zero failures by attributing both to load, on the strength of a standalone recheck (head-importers-flake-recheck.log, '2 passed' EXIT=0, 63.23s). The derivation from the two recorded gates is therefore 2, not 0; the flake attribution is plausible (both are >30s pytest-timeout on a git subprocess under concurrent load) but rests on a third log, and a promotion reader comparing the recorded gates against a count of 0 sees a gap unless the recheck is read too. Neither id reaches the docs-only delta.
